heading: INT. LINCOLN HIGH SCHOOL - GIRLS' BATHROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. LINCOLN HIGH SCHOOL - GIRLS' BATHROOM - DAY
The third-period bell has long since stopped ringing, and the room has settled into that fluorescent hush particular to school plumbing, where every drip is audible and nothing smells quite clean.

THE NURSE, a woman in her fifties with a lanyard she keeps touching as though to confirm she is who it says, kneels beside the farthest stall, speaking in the low, even voice she uses on frightened freshmen, while four girls pretend not to look and a fifth, TESS OKAFOR, sixteen, sits against the tiles with her knees up and her face the colour of paper, insisting for the third time that she just skipped breakfast.
ON PHONE: "tess where r u" / "ms hadley is looking for u" / "u ok??"
That's fine, sweetheart. Skipping breakfast is a very normal thing. Can you let me see your hand?
units.name: THE NURSE

units.text: Tess hides it in her sleeve.

In the mirror, the girl called KIRA, braces, bitten nails, studies the nurse's face, and it is Kira who notices the pale line of tape on the inside of Tess's elbow, a tape that is not from any school infirmary.
She's been doing the thing again, hasn't she.
units.name: KIRA

units.text: No way.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Bea, look at her arm.
units.name: KIRA

units.text: We said we weren't going to tell.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Tell them it's not her fault!
units.name: KIRA

units.text: Don't tell them anything!
units.name: BEA

units.text: The nurse stops.
She looks up at the girls, then down at the girl, and for a long moment the only sound is a faucet losing slowly to gravity.
Which one of you is Ms. Hadley's daughter?
units.name: THE NURSE

units.text: Nobody answers.
Then, from the doorway, a woman in a cardigan, MARGARET HADLEY, forty, stands with her car keys still in hand.
That would be me. Hello, Tess.
units.name: MARGARET

units.text: Margaret, I think we should call an ambulance.
units.name: NURSE

units.text: Mom, I'm sorry.
units.name: TESS
